classes.why: ed3c/noodles#325 subsumes the repository's one concrete single-source rule. The admitted task model was previously guarded by noodles.validate_task_profile_single_source with an exemption list in policy/fitness.json; both are retired into this row, so one implementation judges every registered class.

projections.why: Noodle reads its own routing default before any noodles code runs, so it cannot resolve the pointer; the literal is the handoff to a process that does not read this policy.
The model-eval boundary names the execute model in the argv it refuses to spawn; the refusal has to carry the exact token it is refusing.

classes.why: The provider source URL is the identity half of a pinned external dependency. A second writer is how a retired provider survives in prose: the drift history this atom cites is provider pins copied into the README. Registered with no projections because this tree measurably has none - the detector was run against the rebased head and only the owner carries these URLs.

The exact 40-hex commit is what makes a provider pinned rather than floating. What this row refuses: a file outside the registry that writes one of the lock's commits, and an admitted projection that has fallen off the owner entirely by carrying none of its current commits. What it does NOT refuse, measured on this tree rather than assumed away: a projection citing several pins where only one moved still carries a live sibling value and stays green, because admission is per projection, not per value, and the registry declares no value SHAPE - so a stale 40-hex string inside an otherwise-current projection is invisible here. That partial staleness is the drift a README citing several pins actually produces, and it is a review concern until a per-value rule with a declared shape lands. The refusal is not hypothetical: rebasing this atom onto a default branch it was authored before turned it red, because two projections this row once admitted - migrations/skills-shared/ledger.json, whose source_commit pins a skills-shared tree rather than a provider entry, and tests/test_noodles.py, whose literal lock mirror ed3c/noodles#301 replaced with a retired-name scan - had both stopped carrying any commit this lock currently holds. The detector named them; they are retired here rather than in prose.

projections.why: The context-closure source table cites the exact pinned bytes it read. It is a projection of the lock, and when the lock moves this row makes the citation say so instead of silently describing a commit nobody fetches.

classes.why: The tree-sitter library and grammar commits. Registered with no projections on purpose: this class is the positive control that a clean class exists, so a green detector is not evidence that every class merely has a long exemption list.
